title: A plant for snakebite
translation: There's a plant called menamomi. If a viper bites you, crush some of it and put it on the bite, and it heals right away, they say. Worth learning to recognise.
original: めなもみといふ{草|くさ}あり。
{蝮|くちばみ}にさされたる{人|ひと}、かの{草|くさ}を{揉|も}みてつけぬれば、すなはち{癒|い}ゆとなむ。
literal: There is a plant called menamomi.
If a person who has been bitten by a viper crushes that plant and applies it, he is healed at once, they say.
One should get to know it by sight.

notes.text: Usually identified as the plant still called メナモミ in Japanese (Siegesbeckia pubescens), a weedy relative of the daisy with sticky flower heads. It was used in folk medicine.
{蝮|くちばみ}: an old name for the mamushi, Japan's most common venomous snake. Modern Japanese reads the same kanji まむし.
さす: 'to sting, to pierce'. Older Japanese used it for snakebites as well as insect stings.
すなはち: 'at once'. となむ: 'so it is said', with the end of the sentence (いふ) left out. Kenkō passes it on as something he heard.
べし: 'should'. The whole section is three sentences long and ends on this practical tip.
